title: Optimizely Attack Hits Zoom, BBC, CNN With Skimmer, iOS Kits
content_md: An Optimizely supply chain attack on November 16, 2026, turned a trusted experimentation script into a malware delivery channel for some of the world’s best-known websites. For nearly 19 hours, visitors to sites such as Zoom, BBC, CNN, IKEA, HSBC and Equifax loaded code that swapped cryptocurrency addresses, skimmed payment cards and pushed iOS exploit kits to iPhone and iPad users. Scott Helme of Report URI reported finding 188 infected snippets belonging to 178 organizations. Optimizely confirmed in a status notice that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. How Did a Legitimate Optimizely Snippet Start Serving Malware? Sites that use Optimizely Web load a per-customer JavaScript snippet from cdn.optimizely.com to run A/B tests and personalization. Inside each snippet sits an optional Project JavaScript setting, where customers can add their own code to execute site-wide. The attacker planted a small loader in that setting across many unrelated customer projects. Nothing else in the snippets changed, so browsers kept receiving what looked like a normal Optimizely file from the usual CDN host, under Optimize
